title: Comparing BNF Recursion and EBNF While-Loop Recognizers
description: Recognize comma-separated lists of numbers using both a recursive BNF tail function and an iterative EBNF while loop.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Lines 4-24 implement the BNF grammar (`list -> item list_tail`, `list_tail -> ',' item list_tail | epsilon`). `bnf_list` calls `bnf_item(tokens, 0)` followed by `bnf_list_tail(tokens, pos)`. In `bnf_list_tail`, if `tokens[pos] == ","` and a valid `bnf_item` follows at `pos + 1`, line 23 recurses with `bnf_list_tail(tokens, pos2)`. Otherwise it returns `pos` unchanged (the epsilon case).

`ebnf_list(tokens)` implements `list -> item { ',' item }` in a single function. Lines 28-30 match the first `"NUM"` at index `0` and set `pos = 1`. Lines 31-36 loop while `tokens[pos] == ","` and `tokens[pos + 1] == "NUM"`, advancing `pos += 2`.

Compare `bnf_list_tail` (lines 17-24) with the `while` loop in `ebnf_list` (lines 31-36). BNF expresses repetition with a helper nonterminal that recurses on `pos2` and uses epsilon (`return pos`) to stop. EBNF expresses `{ ',' item }` as a `while` loop.
Lines 39-56 run both `bnf_list` and `ebnf_list` on seven token sequences and check whether their boolean answers agree on every row.

steps.question: On the `"trailing comma"` test case `["NUM", ","]` (line 44), what value of `pos` do `bnf_list_tail` (lines 19-22) and `ebnf_list` (lines 31-35) end up with, and why do both return `False`?
steps.answer: Both consume the first `"NUM"` (`pos = 1`) and see the comma at index `1`. They find no `"NUM"` at index `2` (`pos2 is None` on line 21 / `pos + 1 >= len(tokens)` on line 34). Both stop at `pos = 1`. Since `len(tokens)` is `2`, `pos == len(tokens)` (`1 == 2`) is `False` in both.

steps.description: At trace step 50 on `['NUM', ',', 'NUM']`, `bnf_list_tail` has matched `','` at index `1` and `'NUM'` at index `2` (`pos2 = 3`). Line 23 recurses with `bnf_list_tail(tokens, 3)`.
